chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard my father say: 'Part of the beauty of a person's Islam is leaving that which does not concern him.'

key_terms.مَا لَا يَعْنِيهِ: That which does not concern him

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for something to be 'not concerning' a person in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: In the context of *Kitab al-Zuhd*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines 'good Islam' not merely as ritual observance but as social and spiritual discipline, specifically the restraint of the tongue from irrelevant matters. This principle serves as a foundational criterion for distinguishing the pious from the noisy, emphasizing that guarding against the trivial is essential for preserving spiritual focus and social harmony.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 19.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said, “
I heard my father say, ‘It is from the beauty of a person’s [devotion to] Islam to eschew that which does not concern him.’”
